notes:
Design partner for Route-level A/B testing (Console > Rollouts > Route experiments). Primary goal is to A/B model variants for their support-agent route with deterministic user assignment and clear guardrails.

Account snapshot
- Product: multi-tenant support automation app (agentic workflows). Heavy chat completions + occasional embeddings for retrieval.
- Current inference posture: mix of 3P APIs + some self-hosted GPU for peak. Wants to consolidate onto Redwood if unit economics + reliability are predictable.
- Deployment: prefers Redwood Dedicated in customer VPC long-term; beta running on Hosted API w/ strict data handling. Initial region: us-east-1; wants eu-west-1 option for EU customers later.

Route experiments requirements (from calls + beta kickoff)
- Needs route-level experiments on a single endpoint (their /agent/respond) with 2-3 variants.
- Variants are primarily different models and/or quantization profiles:
  - Variant A: “baseline” (current prod model profile)
  - Variant B: candidate model w/ lower cost
  - (Optional) Variant C: higher-quality model for difficult tickets
- Deterministic assignment:
  - Must be sticky by end-user (they can pass stable end_user_id). Cannot rely on IP; session cookies sometimes absent due to embedded widgets.
  - Asked for explicit guidance on stickiness key precedence and what happens when key missing (they saw skew in a different vendor).
- Guardrails (beta expectations):
  - Wants near-real-time guardrails for p95/p99 latency + error rate; prefers soft-stop w/ clear alerting first.
  - Target thresholds discussed (for their baseline traffic): p95 < 450ms, p99 < 900ms at steady state; error rate < 0.5%.
  - Cost: watches cost per 1k output tokens + total $/day. Wants alerts when cost delta exceeds +10% without quality improvement.
- Measurement expectations:
  - Needs per-variant breakdown by route + region.
  - Wants ability to drill down into “why variant was assigned” when debugging (headers acceptable; also asked for a debug endpoint for support).
  - Quality: interested in Redwood eval signals later; for beta, they’re OK with proxy metrics + a small manual review set.

Security/compliance notes
- SOC 2 required.
- SSO/SAML required for Console access (admin + break-glass).
- Audit logging: emphasized that experiment config changes are production-impacting; wants exportable audit trail with actor identity + change diff.
- Data residency: for EU customers, they need eu-west processing; asked whether experiments guarantee cross-region deterministic bucketing (same user -> same variant in both regions). We explained deterministic bucketing is consistent if stickiness key is stable and hash logic matches.

Activity timeline (recent)
- 2025-01-09: Intro + positioning call (PLG motion, but they want Dedicated pricing early). Identified A/B testing as a must-have for rollout.
- 2025-02-06: Beta technical deep dive (Fireflies transcript linked). Key outcomes:
  - Confirmed stickiness key will be end_user_id (passed by their backend).
  - Agreed on initial experiment: 90/10 split baseline vs candidate.
  - Asked that Console show both absolute metrics + deltas and make it obvious when attribution is missing.
- 2025-02-14: Enabled beta feature flag on staging; validated variant headers in responses.
- 2025-02-26: Noted intermittent missing experiment attribution on streaming retries; Logan/Caleb pulled traces; linked to SUP-24877 (tracked across a few beta accounts).
- 2025-03-04: POC check-in (shared learnings from other beta):
  - They reported Console results sometimes lagging by 30-60+ minutes; they can tolerate some delay but want an explicit “data freshness” indicator + propagation/aggregation status. Related to SUP-24910.
  - Requested guardrail defaults to be editable per route because they have different SLOs for “chat” vs “summarize.”

Open questions / risks (internal)
- They will push for Dedicated/VPC before scaling beyond 25% traffic. Need pricing + capacity plan.
- They are sensitive to metrics cardinality cost. Ensure route_id is normalized (template path, not raw) and confirm the experiment tag restrictions/sampling.
- If audit export isn’t ready, security will block procurement. Need to provide evidence: sample audit event payload, retention, and export mechanism.
